title: No PHP-style name aliasing; `type` aliases are the disciplined exception
scope:
`class_alias()`; the `use X as Y;` import form for classes, interfaces and enums; and, as the
one thing this ADR *adds* rather than removes, a new `type Name = TypeExpr;` declaration. Not in scope:
trait composition, which has no aliasing rule to state because
[0043](0043.md) leaves no trait.

summary.headline: Nothing gets a second name, except a `type` alias for a shape
summary.body:
A class, interface, enum, method or constant is reachable under the name it was declared with —
short or fully qualified — and under no other. There is no `class_alias()`, and `use Foo\Bar as
Baz;` does not compile. What survives is a `type` alias, such as `type UserId = uint;` or `type
Row = array<string, int|string>;`: a synonym for a type expression that the checker resolves and
nothing at run time ever sees. An alias may not name a single bare class, which would be import
renaming through a different door.
